items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: You turn on the radio, or put on a Frank Sinatra record, and play along with it

ctx.x: Well gee, faking tunes you don’t know on the bass, I mean that’s about as hard as you could get.

Well that’s a kind of a curse of the instrument though. I mean even though say at a party like this, you’ll go up and the horn players will call a tune, and if the piano player knows it, or the guitarist knows it, you’re going to play it. They’re not going to not play it if you say well gee I’m not sure about this. “Oh, you’ll hear it,” you know. And that’s kind of the nature of the instrument. And I tell my students that. You turn on the radio, or put on a Frank Sinatra record, and play along with it, and try to…
Along with carting your instrument around.
